questions.q: In a sentence with both object pronouns, the _____ comes first.
questions.why_correct: The indirect object pronoun (me, te, se, nos) always precedes the direct object pronoun (lo, la, los, las).
why_wrong: The direct object pronoun always comes second.
Subject pronouns are separate from object pronouns.
Reflexive pronouns are a different concept.

questions.q: "Le" changes to "se" when it comes before _____.
questions.why_correct: Le and les both change to se before lo, la, los, las to avoid awkward pronunciation.
why_wrong: Me and te never trigger this change.
The change happens before another pronoun, not a verb.
Two IO pronouns wouldn't appear together.
questions.tip: le/les → se before lo, la, los, las.

questions.q: In "Yo se lo di," what does "se" replace?
questions.why_correct: Se replaces le (or les) when followed by lo, la, los, or las.
why_wrong: Lo is the direct object pronoun in this sentence.
Me is 1st person — se replaces 3rd person le/les.
Les also changes to se before a direct object pronoun.
questions.tip: se = le or les in combined pronouns.

questions.q: In "Me la trajo," what does "la" represent?
questions.why_correct: La is a direct object pronoun (feminine singular). Me is the indirect object.
why_wrong: Me is the indirect object pronoun here.
Neither pronoun is the subject.
La is always a direct object pronoun.
questions.tip: In IOP + DOP: first = indirect, second = direct.

questions.q: Yo di la ensalada al camarero. → Yo _____ di.
questions.why_correct: Al camarero → le → se (before la); la ensalada → la. Combined: se la.
why_wrong: Le la is never correct — le becomes se before la.
Me = to me; the recipient is the waiter.
IO always comes before DO.

questions.q: Ellos pasaron los papeles a ti. → Ellos _____ pasaron.
questions.why_correct: A ti → te (IOP); los papeles → los (DOP). Combined: te los.
why_wrong: IO always comes before DO.
Se replaces le/les, not te.
Las is feminine — papeles is masculine plural.

questions.q: Nosotros trajimos las pizzas a los chicos. → Nosotros _____ trajimos.
questions.why_correct: A los chicos → les → se (before las); las pizzas → las. Combined: se las.
why_wrong: Les las is never correct — les becomes se before las.
Nos = to us; the recipients are los chicos.
Los is masculine — pizzas is feminine plural.

questions.q: Tú nunca revelaste el secreto a mí. → Tú nunca _____ revelaste.
questions.why_correct: A mí → me (IOP); el secreto → lo (DOP). Combined: me lo.
why_wrong: IO always comes before DO.
Se replaces le/les — me stays as me.
Te = to you; the recipient is me.

questions.q: Mis hermanas dieron los regalos a mí. → Mis hermanas _____ dieron.
questions.why_correct: A mí → me (IOP); los regalos → los (DOP). Combined: me los.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not me.
Te = to you — the recipient is me.
Las is feminine — regalos is masculine plural.

questions.q: Yo decía la verdad a mi madre. → Yo _____ decía.
questions.why_correct: A mi madre → le → se (before la); la verdad → la. Combined: se la.
why_wrong: Le la is never correct — le becomes se before la.
Nos = to us; the recipient is the mother.
Me = to me; the recipient is the mother.

questions.q: Él compró los zapatos para ti. → Él _____ compró.
questions.why_correct: Para ti → te (IOP); los zapatos → los (DOP). Combined: te los.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only — te stays.
Me = to me — the recipient is you.
Las is feminine — zapatos is masculine plural.

questions.q: Mamá preparó la cena para nosotros. → Mamá _____ preparó.
questions.why_correct: Para nosotros → nos (IOP); la cena → la (DOP). Combined: nos la.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les — nos stays.
Lo is masculine — cena is feminine.
Me = to me; the recipient is us.

questions.q: El maestro explicó la lección a los estudiantes. → El maestro _____ explicó.
questions.why_correct: A los estudiantes → les → se (before la); la lección → la. Combined: se la.
why_wrong: Les la is never correct — les becomes se before la.
Nos = to us; the recipients are the students.
Me = to me; the recipients are the students.

questions.q: Yo leí el cuento a los niños. → Yo _____ leí.
questions.why_correct: A los niños → les → se (before lo); el cuento → lo. Combined: se lo.
why_wrong: Les lo is never correct — les becomes se before lo.
Me = to me; the recipients are the children.
Nos = to us; the recipients are the children.

questions.q: IO "me" + DO "la" = _____
questions.why_correct: Me (IO) + la (DO) = me la. Me does not change.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only.
IO always comes before DO.
Lo is masculine.

questions.q: IO "le" + DO "lo" = _____
questions.why_correct: Le changes to se before lo, la, los, las. Le + lo = se lo.
why_wrong: Le lo is never correct.
IO always comes before DO.
La is feminine.

questions.q: IO "nos" + DO "los" = _____
questions.why_correct: Nos (IO) + los (DO) = nos los. Nos does not change.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only.
IO always comes before DO.
Lo is singular — use los for plural.

questions.q: IO "les" + DO "las" = _____
questions.why_correct: Les changes to se before las. Les + las = se las.
why_wrong: Les las is never correct.
IO always comes before DO.
Los is masculine plural.

questions.q: IO "te" + DO "la" = _____
questions.why_correct: Te (IO) + la (DO) = te la. Te does not change.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only.
IO always comes before DO.
Lo is masculine.

questions.q: IO "me" + DO "los" = _____
questions.why_correct: Me (IO) + los (DO) = me los. Me does not change.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only.
IO always comes before DO.
Las is feminine plural.

questions.q: IO "te" + DO "lo" = _____
questions.why_correct: Te (IO) + lo (DO) = te lo. Te does not change.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only.
IO always comes before DO.
La is feminine.

questions.q: IO "le" + DO "las" = _____
questions.why_correct: Le changes to se before las. Le + las = se las.
why_wrong: Le las is never correct.
IO always comes before DO.
Los is masculine plural.

questions.q: IO "nos" + DO "la" = _____
questions.why_correct: Nos (IO) + la (DO) = nos la. Nos does not change.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only.
IO always comes before DO.
Lo is masculine.

questions.q: IO "les" + DO "lo" = _____
questions.why_correct: Les changes to se before lo. Les + lo = se lo.
why_wrong: Les lo is never correct.
IO always comes before DO.
La is feminine.

questions.q: IO "te" + DO "las" = _____
questions.why_correct: Te (IO) + las (DO) = te las. Te does not change.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les only.
IO always comes before DO.
Los is masculine plural.

questions.q: IO "le" + DO "lo" + IO "le" before DO → _____
questions.why_correct: Le must always change to se when directly before lo, la, los, or las.
why_wrong: Le lo is never a valid combination.
IO always precedes DO.
Se is the IO, lo is the DO — IO comes first.
questions.tip: le before any DO pronoun → se.

questions.q: "I gave it (masc.) to you (tú)." → _____
questions.why_correct: A ti → te (IOP); it masc. → lo (DOP). Verb: di (yo, preterite of dar).
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not te.
Me = to me — the recipient is you.
IO always comes before DO.

questions.q: "She told it (fem.) to us." → _____
questions.why_correct: To us → nos (IOP); it fem. → la (DOP). Verb: dijo (ella, preterite of decir).
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not nos.
Me = to me — the recipient is us.
IO always comes before DO.

questions.q: "He sent them (masc.) to her." → _____
questions.why_correct: To her → le → se (before los); them masc. → los. Verb: mandó.
why_wrong: Le los is never correct — le becomes se before los.
IO always comes before DO.
Nos = to us — the recipient is her.

questions.q: "You (tú) never told it (masc.) to me." → _____
questions.why_correct: Nunca + me (IO) + lo (DO) + verb. Adverb goes before the pronouns.
why_wrong: Nunca precedes the pronouns, not the verb.
IO always comes before DO.
Se replaces le/les — me stays as me.
questions.tip: Word order: nunca + IOP + DOP + verb.

questions.q: "We showed it (fem.) to you (tú)." → _____
questions.why_correct: A ti → te (IOP); it fem. → la (DOP). Verb: mostramos (nosotros).
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not te.
Me = to me; the recipient is you.
Nos = to us; the recipient is you.

questions.q: "They gave them (fem.) to us." → _____
questions.why_correct: To us → nos (IOP); them fem. → las (DOP). Verb: dieron (ellos).
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not nos.
Me = to me; the recipients are us.
Los is masculine plural.
questions.tip: to us = nos; fem. plural = las.

questions.q: "I want to send it (masc.) to them." → _____
questions.why_correct: To them → les → se (before lo); it masc. → lo. Combined: se lo.
why_wrong: Les lo is never correct — les becomes se before lo.
Te = to you; the recipients are them.
Me = to me; the recipients are them.

questions.q: "Can you (tú) bring it (masc.) to me?" → _____
questions.why_correct: To me → me (IOP); it masc. → lo (DOP). Pronouns go before the auxiliary.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not me.
La is feminine — use lo for masculine.
IO always comes before DO.
questions.tip: With auxiliary verbs: IOP + DOP before the auxiliary.

questions.q: Nosotros dimos el dinero a ustedes. → Nosotros _____ dimos.
questions.why_correct: A ustedes → les → se (before lo); el dinero → lo. Combined: se lo.
why_wrong: Les lo is never correct — les becomes se before lo.
Nos = to us; the recipients are ustedes.
Te = to you (tú); the recipients are ustedes.

questions.q: Ella trajo las flores a mí. → Ella _____ trajo.
questions.why_correct: A mí → me (IOP); las flores → las (DOP). Combined: me las.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not me.
Te = to you; the recipient is me.
Los is masculine — flores is feminine plural.

questions.q: Tú mandaste el mensaje a nosotros. → Tú _____ mandaste.
questions.why_correct: A nosotros → nos (IOP); el mensaje → lo (DOP). Combined: nos lo.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not nos.
Me = to me; the recipients are nosotros.
La is feminine — mensaje is masculine.

questions.q: El chef preparó los tacos para ellos. → El chef _____ preparó.
questions.why_correct: Para ellos → les → se (before los); los tacos → los. Combined: se los.
why_wrong: Les los is never correct — les becomes se before los.
Me = to me; the recipients are ellos.
Nos = to us; the recipients are ellos.

questions.q: Papá contó el chiste a ti. → Papá _____ contó.
questions.why_correct: A ti → te (IOP); el chiste → lo (DOP). Combined: te lo.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not te.
Me = to me; the recipient is ti.
La is feminine — chiste is masculine.

questions.q: Mi amiga prestó los apuntes a mí. → Mi amiga _____ prestó.
questions.why_correct: A mí → me (IOP); los apuntes → los (DOP). Combined: me los.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not me.
Te = to you; the recipient is me.
Las is feminine — apuntes is masculine plural.

questions.q: Ustedes explicaron el problema a nosotros. → Ustedes _____ explicaron.
questions.why_correct: A nosotros → nos (IOP); el problema → lo (DOP). Combined: nos lo.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not nos.
Me = to me; the recipients are nosotros.
La is feminine — problema is masculine.

questions.q: Mi hermano mandó las fotos a ti. → Mi hermano _____ mandó.
questions.why_correct: A ti → te (IOP); las fotos → las (DOP). Combined: te las.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not te.
Me = to me; the recipient is ti.
Los is masculine — fotos is feminine plural.

questions.q: Yo vendo el coche a él. → Yo _____ vendo.
questions.why_correct: A él → le → se (before lo); el coche → lo. Combined: se lo.
why_wrong: Le lo is never correct — le becomes se before lo.
Me = to me; the recipient is él.
Nos = to us; the recipient is él.

questions.q: Ella siempre compra flores para él. → Ella siempre _____ compra.
questions.why_correct: Para él → le → se (before las); las flores → las. Combined: se las.
why_wrong: Le las is never correct — le becomes se before las.
Me = to me; the recipient is él.
Los is masculine — flores is feminine plural.
questions.tip: para él = le → se; flores = las.

questions.q: La tienda envió los paquetes a nosotros. → La tienda _____ envió.
questions.why_correct: A nosotros → nos (IOP); los paquetes → los (DOP). Combined: nos los.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not nos.
Me = to me; the recipients are nosotros.
Las is feminine — paquetes is masculine plural.

questions.q: El médico recetó las pastillas a ella. → El médico _____ recetó.
questions.why_correct: A ella → le → se (before las); las pastillas → las. Combined: se las.
why_wrong: Le las is never correct — le becomes se before las.
Me = to me; the recipient is ella.
Los is masculine — pastillas is feminine plural.
questions.tip: a ella = le → se; pastillas = las.

questions.q: Mi madre enseñó la receta a mí. → Mi madre _____ enseñó.
questions.why_correct: A mí → me (IOP); la receta → la (DOP). Combined: me la.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not me.
Te = to you; the recipient is me.
Lo is masculine — receta is feminine.

questions.q: Los estudiantes hicieron preguntas al maestro. → Los estudiantes _____ hicieron.
questions.why_correct: Al maestro → le → se (before las); las preguntas → las. Combined: se las.
why_wrong: Les las is never correct — les becomes se before las.
Me = to me; the recipient is el maestro.
Los is masculine — preguntas is feminine plural.
questions.tip: al maestro = le → se; preguntas = las.

questions.q: Tú me diste tu número. Replace the direct object: Tú _____ diste.
questions.why_correct: Me stays (IO = to me); tu número → lo (masculine singular DO). Combined: me lo.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les — me stays.
IO always comes before DO.
Te = to you; the recipient is me.

questions.q: Carlos va a prestar el libro a mí. → Carlos _____ va a prestar.
questions.why_correct: A mí → me (IOP); el libro → lo (DOP). Pronouns go before the auxiliary va.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not me.
La is feminine — libro is masculine.
Te = to you; the recipient is me.
questions.tip: Pronouns go before the auxiliary verb.

questions.q: In a negative sentence, combined pronouns go _____.
questions.why_correct: Word order: no + IOP + DOP + verb. Example: No me lo digas.
why_wrong: Pronouns always follow the negation word.
Pronouns precede the conjugated verb.
The two pronouns always stay together.

questions.q: "Ella me lo compró" means _____.
questions.why_correct: Ella = she (subject); me = to/for me (IO); lo = it, masculine (DO); compró = bought.
why_wrong: The subject is ella, not yo.
Lo is masculine — la would be feminine.
Me is the recipient, not the thing bought.

questions.q: "Ella nos lo dijo" means _____.
questions.why_correct: Ella = she; nos = to us (IO); lo = it (DO); dijo = told.
why_wrong: Nos = to us, not him.
The subject is ella, not we.
Nos = to us, not to them.

questions.q: "Yo te lo prometo" means _____.
questions.why_correct: Yo = I; te = to you (IO); lo = it (DO); prometo = I promise.
why_wrong: Yo = I; prometo = 1st person present.
Yo = I, not he.
Lo specifies 'it' as the direct object.

questions.q: "Nos las enviaron" means _____.
questions.why_correct: Nos = to us (IO); las = them, feminine (DO); enviaron = they sent.
why_wrong: Nos = to us; enviaron = they.
Las = feminine plural — use los for masculine.
Enviaron = they (plural), not she.

questions.q: "¿Cuándo me lo vas a decir?" means _____.
questions.correct: When are you going to tell it to me?
incorrect: When am I going to tell it to you?
When is he going to tell me?
Are you going to tell me when?
questions.why_correct: Me = to me (IO); lo = it (DO); vas a decir = you're going to tell.
why_wrong: Vas = you're going to — not I.
Me = to me; lo = it (DO is present).
It's a question word (cuándo), not a yes/no question.
questions.tip: me lo = it to me; vas = you (tú).

questions.q: "Te la traje ayer" — which word order is correct?
questions.why_correct: IO (te) + DO (la) both come before the conjugated verb (traje).
why_wrong: IO always precedes DO.
Both pronouns go before the verb, not after.
Both pronouns must stay together before the verb.
questions.tip: IOP + DOP always together, before the verb.

questions.q: Which sentence has an error?
questions.why_correct: Le before lo is incorrect — le must change to se: Yo se lo di.
why_wrong: Te la is correct (te + la).
Nos los is correct (nos + los).
Me la is correct (me + la).
questions.tip: le + lo is always wrong — use se lo.

questions.q: Which sentence has an error?
questions.why_correct: Les las is incorrect — les must change to se before las: se las.
why_wrong: Se las is correct (les → se before las).
Me lo is correct (me + lo).
Te lo is correct (te + lo).
questions.tip: les + las is always wrong — use se las.

questions.q: When do we use "se" in combined pronouns?
questions.why_correct: Only le (3rd person singular) and les (3rd person plural) change to se before lo/la/los/las.
why_wrong: 1st person uses me, which never changes.
2nd person uses te, which never changes.
Nos and te keep their forms.

questions.q: In "Te los mandé," the subject is _____.
questions.why_correct: "Mandé" is 1st person singular preterite (yo). Te = to you (IO), los = them (DO).
why_wrong: Tú would use mandaste.
Ellos would use mandaron.
Él would use mandó.

questions.q: "Quiero darte los zapatos." With combined pronouns attached to the infinitive: _____
questions.why_correct: Combined pronouns attach to the END of the infinitive: dar + te + los = dártelos (written accent added).
why_wrong: Pronouns attach at the end of the infinitive, not before it.
Placing them before the auxiliary is also valid, but not the only option.
Pronouns must attach directly to the infinitive end.
questions.tip: Attach to end of infinitive: dár-te-los.

questions.q: "Voy a mostrarte el proyecto." Rewrite with combined pronouns on the infinitive: _____
questions.why_correct: Mostrar + te + lo = mostrártelo (accent on the stressed syllable).
why_wrong: Pronouns attach at the end of the infinitive.
The combined form replaces the separate pronouns.
Pronouns attach directly to the infinitive end.

questions.q: In affirmative commands, combined pronouns go _____.
questions.correct: attached to the end of the command
incorrect: after a comma following the verb
questions.why_correct: With affirmative commands, pronouns attach to the end: Dámelo (da + me + lo).
why_wrong: Pronouns precede the verb in negative commands, not affirmative ones.
There is no comma — pronouns attach directly.
The two pronouns always stay together.
questions.tip: Affirmative command + IOP + DOP attached at end.

questions.q: In negative commands, combined pronouns go _____.
incorrect: attached to the end of the verb
questions.why_correct: Negative commands: no + IOP + DOP + verb. Example: No me lo digas.
why_wrong: Attaching to the end is only for affirmative commands.
Pronouns precede the conjugated command verb.
Pronouns follow "no" in negative commands.

questions.why_correct: Da (affirmative command) + me (IO) + lo (DO) = dámelo.
why_wrong: IO comes before DO, even when attached.
Se replaces le/les — me stays.
Lo is masculine — use la for feminine.

questions.q: "No se lo digas" — which type of command is this?
questions.why_correct: No + se lo + digas: negative command. Digas is the tú subjunctive form.
why_wrong: Affirmative commands have pronouns attached to the end.
Nosotros command would use digamos.
Usted command would use diga.

questions.q: To clarify who "se" refers to, we can add _____ to the sentence.
questions.correct: a él / a ella / a usted / a ellos
questions.why_correct: Se can mean le (him, her, you formal) or les (them, you all). A prepositional phrase clarifies the recipient.
why_wrong: A mí and a nosotros go with me and nos, not se.
A ti and a vosotros go with te and os, not se.
Se is often ambiguous without a clarifying phrase.
questions.tip: Add a + pronoun/noun to clarify se.

questions.q: "Se lo expliqué a los estudiantes." The phrase "a los estudiantes" _____.
incorrect: is redundant and should be removed
questions.why_correct: Se can be ambiguous (him, her, them, you). The a-phrase makes clear the recipient is los estudiantes.
why_wrong: Se must still appear — the a-phrase only clarifies.
The a-phrase is helpful and commonly used for clarity.
Lo refers to the direct object, unaffected by the a-phrase.

questions.q: Which group of pronouns can be the IO in a combined pair?
questions.why_correct: Indirect object pronouns are me (yo), te (tú), se (él/ella/ud./ellos), nos (nosotros).
why_wrong: Lo, la, los, las are direct object pronouns.
Yo, tú, él, ella are subject pronouns.
Lo is a direct object pronoun, not indirect.
questions.tip: IO: me, te, se, nos. DO: lo, la, los, las.

questions.q: Which group of pronouns can be the DO in a combined pair?
questions.why_correct: Direct object pronouns are lo (masc. sg.), la (fem. sg.), los (masc. pl.), las (fem. pl.).
why_wrong: Me, te, se, nos are indirect object pronouns.
Yo, tú, él, ella are subject pronouns.
Se and me are indirect; le is replaced by se.

questions.q: "Mis padres me la regalaron." "Me la" means _____.
questions.why_correct: Me = to me (IO); la = it, feminine (DO). Regalaron = they gave as a gift.
why_wrong: Me is the indirect object here, not direct.
La is feminine — lo would be masculine.
Me = to me (recipient), not from me.

questions.q: "¿Por qué no me lo dijiste?" means _____.
questions.correct: Why didn't you tell it to me?
incorrect: Why didn't I tell it to you?
questions.why_correct: Me = to me (IO); lo = it (DO); dijiste = you told (tú, preterite).
why_wrong: Dijiste = you (tú), not I.
Lo = it (DO is present); me = to me.
Lo confirms 'it' is the direct object.
questions.tip: me lo = it to me; dijiste = you told.

questions.q: Rewrite: "Ellos quieren mandarme las flores." → _____
questions.why_correct: A mí → me; las flores → las. Combined: me las. Pronouns go before the auxiliary quieren.
why_wrong: Les las is never correct — les becomes se.
Se replaces le/les, not me.
Los is masculine — flores is feminine plural.
questions.tip: Detach from infinitive and place before auxiliary.

questions.q: "¿Me puedes dar el número?" → with combined pronouns: _____
questions.why_correct: Me stays (IO); el número → lo (masculine DO). Combined: me lo.
why_wrong: Le lo is never correct — use se lo for 3rd person.
La is feminine — número is masculine.
IO always comes before DO.

questions.q: "¿Puedes prestarme los apuntes?" → pronouns before auxiliary: _____
questions.why_correct: Me stays (IO); los apuntes → los (DO). Combined: me los before the auxiliary puedes.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not me.
Las is feminine — apuntes is masculine plural.
IO always comes before DO.
questions.tip: Detach pronouns and place before the auxiliary.

questions.q: "Estoy haciéndotelo" = estoy + haciendo + _____ + _____
questions.why_correct: Haciendo + te (IO) + lo (DO) = haciéndotelo. IO attaches first, then DO.
why_wrong: IO attaches before DO.
Se replaces le/les — te stays.
Me = to me; the recipient is tú.
questions.tip: Gerund + IO + DO attached at end.

questions.q: "Ella está explicándoselo a los niños." What does "se" replace?
questions.why_correct: A los niños → les → se (before lo). Combined: se lo, attached to the gerund.
why_wrong: Me = 1st person; the recipients are the children.
Nos = 1st person plural; the recipients are the children.
Te = 2nd person; the recipients are the children.

questions.q: "Se la voy a comprar a mi abuela." The phrase "a mi abuela" tells us _____.
questions.why_correct: Se can mean le (him, her, you formal) or les. "A mi abuela" clarifies the recipient is la abuela.
why_wrong: La is the direct object — "a mi abuela" is the indirect object clarifier.
The a-phrase identifies who, not why.
Voy a indicates timing — a mi abuela specifies the recipient.
questions.tip: a + person clarifies who se refers to.

questions.q: Complete: "¿Quién _____ explicó la tarea?" (to you, tú)
questions.why_correct: To you (tú) → te (IO); la tarea → la (DO). Combined: te la.
why_wrong: Se replaces le/les, not te.
Me = to me; the recipient is tú.
Le la is never correct.
